description: Our first contestant should look familiar, because it's you, about 300,000 years ago. Same face, slightly longer head. No idea what tonight has in store. Let's ease in.
facts: The oldest Homo sapiens fossils found so far come from Jebel Irhoud in Morocco, not East Africa, and are about 315,000 years old.
Their faces already fall within the range of people alive today, but their braincases were longer and lower than ours.
punchline: Cutting this one means breaking up with your own species. Bold opener.

anatomy.female: Dark brown skin, short tightly curled black hair, little body hair. About 1.60 m and 54 kg, slim and long-limbed with modern proportions, fully upright. Modern face with a small chin and a faint brow ridge; braincase slightly longer and lower than today's. Wears a tanned hide wrap fully covering the chest and a hide loincloth.
anatomy.male: Dark brown skin, short tightly curled black hair and a short beard, light body hair. About 1.72 m and 65 kg, lean and muscular, long legs, modern proportions, fully upright. Modern face with a defined chin and a slight brow ridge; braincase slightly longer and lower than today's. Bare-chested, wearing a tanned hide loincloth.

sources.claim: Thermoluminescence dating puts the Jebel Irhoud fossils at about 315,000 years old, the oldest known Homo sapiens.
Jebel Irhoud fossils are the earliest known Homo sapiens, found in Morocco rather than East Africa.
Jebel Irhoud faces are modern while the braincase is archaic and elongated.

description: Next up, one of our two closest relatives. The other is waiting backstage. Neanderthals lived across Ice Age Europe and western and central Asia, shorter and stockier than us and built for the cold. They also have history with your family, so play nice.
facts: Neanderthal brains were as large as ours, and often larger.
Most people outside Africa carry 1 to 2% Neanderthal DNA. One 2024 study traces most of it to a stretch of mixing that began around 50,000 years ago and lasted about 7,000 years.
The oldest known evidence of anyone making fire, about 400,000 years old, comes from Barnham in England, and researchers think early Neanderthals lit it.
punchline: Some of your ancestors already said yes. You inherited the receipts.

anatomy.female: Light skin with freckles and straight auburn-red hair (genes suggest some had pale skin and red hair); modest body hair. About 1.55 m and 54 kg, stocky and very strong: wide barrel chest, wide hips, short forearms and shins, large hands. Long low skull, rounded double-arched brow ridge jutting over the eyes, projecting midface, very large wide nose, weak chin. Wears a simple hide wrap fully covering the chest and a hide loincloth.
anatomy.male: Light olive skin, weathered; dark brown hair and full beard; moderate body hair on chest, arms and legs. About 1.65 m and 65 kg, barrel-chested and heavily muscled, short forearms and shins, thick joints, large hands. Long low skull, heavy double-arched brow ridge jutting over the eyes, projecting midface, very large wide nose, weak chin. Bare-chested, wearing a fur-trimmed hide loincloth.

sources.claim: Neanderthals lived about 400,000 to 40,000 years ago across Europe and southwestern to central Asia; their brains were as large as ours and often larger.
Non-Africans carry 1-2% Neanderthal DNA; the main interbreeding began about 50,500 years ago, averaged about 47,000, and lasted about 7,000 years.
Barnham, UK: earliest evidence of fire-making, about 400,000 years old, probably by early Neanderthals.

description: Our mystery guest. For years we knew Denisovans mostly from DNA, a finger bone, a few teeth and a couple of jawbones, until a skull from Harbin in China turned out to be one of them. Tonight, for the first time, they get to show you their face.
facts: In 2025, proteins from the Harbin "Dragon Man" skull and DNA from the tartar on its teeth showed it was Denisovan, and at least 146,000 years old.
A girl from Denisova Cave in Siberia had a Neanderthal mother and a Denisovan father.
Many Tibetans carry a Denisovan version of the EPAS1 gene, which helps people cope with life at high altitude.
punchline: Neanderthal mom, Denisovan dad. Holidays were tense.

anatomy.female: Dark brown skin, dark brown hair and brown eyes, as the Denisova genome suggests; modest body hair. Body barely known: estimated about 1.60 m, robust, broad-shouldered and heavy-boned. Very large, long, low skull, thick brow ridge, broad flat face, wide nose and mouth, very large teeth, no chin. Wears a fur wrap fully covering the chest and a hide loincloth.
anatomy.male: Dark brown skin, dark brown hair and beard, brown eyes, as the Denisova genome suggests; moderate body hair. Body barely known: estimated about 1.70 m, robust, broad and heavily built. Very large, long, low skull like the Harbin skull, heavy brow ridge, broad flat face, wide nose and mouth, very large teeth, no chin. Bare-chested, wearing a fur loincloth.

sources.claim: Harbin skull identified as Denisovan from proteins and dental-calculus mtDNA; at least 146,000 years old.
Denisova 11, a female at least 13 years old, had a Neanderthal mother and a Denisovan father (Slon et al. 2018).
The Tibetan high-altitude EPAS1 variant came from Denisovans.
Xiahe mandible from the Tibetan Plateau identified as Denisovan by ancient proteins.
Penghu 1 mandible from Taiwan identified as a male Denisovan by ancient proteins.
Denisova 25 molar belonged to a Denisovan who lived about 200,000 years ago (preprint, not yet peer-reviewed).
A Denisovan rib from Baishiya Karst Cave dates to about 48,000-32,000 years ago.

description: This one comes with a complicated past. Homo heidelbergensis lived in Africa and Europe and was possibly close to the common ancestor we share with Neanderthals and Denisovans. Some scientists want to retire the name altogether, so tread carefully.
facts: Scientists once filed the skeletons from Spain's Pit of Bones under this species, until their anatomy and then ancient DNA put them on the early Neanderthal line.
A 2021 proposal wanted to drop the name and call the African fossils Homo bodoensis instead.
punchline: Scientists can't agree what to call this one. Sounds like a few of your situationships.

anatomy.female: Warm medium brown skin, dark brown hair, moderate body hair. About 1.57 m and 51 kg, short wide body, broad hips, thick strong limbs, fully upright. Large braincase, very large brow ridge, flatter face than earlier species, broad nose, no chin. Wears a simple hide wrap fully covering the chest and a hide loincloth.
anatomy.male: Warm medium brown skin, dark brown hair and short beard, moderate body hair. About 1.75 m and 62 kg, tall, broad and powerfully built, heavy bones, thick muscular limbs. Large braincase, very large brow ridge, flatter face than earlier species, broad nose, heavy jaw, no chin. Bare-chested, wearing a hide loincloth.

sources.claim: Homo heidelbergensis lived about 700,000 to 200,000 years ago in Africa and Europe.
Sima de los Huesos crania show derived Neanderthal features, placing them at the roots of the Neanderthal lineage.
Nuclear DNA places the Sima de los Huesos hominins on the Neanderthal line.
Roksandic et al. propose Homo bodoensis and suppressing Homo heidelbergensis.

description: Long legs, built for walking, and a serious travel habit. Homo erectus started in Africa and made it as far as Georgia, China and Indonesia. Fair warning: this contestant does not stay in one place.
facts: Homo erectus is generally considered the first species we know of with fossils outside Africa, at Dmanisi in Georgia, about 1.8 million years ago.
It was probably the first species to use fire, but it seems to have carried and kept natural fire rather than making its own.
The species lasted nearly 2 million years, about six times longer than Homo sapiens has been around.
punchline: Went nearly two million years. Can you say the same?

anatomy.female: Dark brown skin, short tightly curled dark hair, little body hair, like ours. About 1.55 m, slender and long-legged with modern body proportions, narrow hips, fully upright. Long low skull, thick straight brow ridge, receding forehead, projecting lower face, broad nose, no chin. Wears a simple hide wrap fully covering the chest and a hide loincloth.
anatomy.male: Dark brown skin, short tightly curled dark hair, sparse beard, little body hair, like ours. About 1.78 m and 60 kg, tall and lean, long legs, narrow hips, a modern-like body like the Turkana Boy skeleton. Long low skull, thick straight brow ridge, receding forehead, projecting lower face, broad nose, no chin. Bare-chested, wearing a hide loincloth.

sources.claim: Homo erectus height range, modern body proportions, range across Africa, Georgia, China and Indonesia; generally considered the first species to expand beyond Africa.
Oldest known Homo erectus (DNH 134, Drimolen) dates to about 2 million years ago.
Last Homo erectus at Ngandong, about 117,000 to 108,000 years ago.
Dmanisi Homo erectus fossils date to 1.85-1.77 million years ago; older tools in China mean someone left Africa earlier.
Wonderwerk Cave fire use 1.07-1.79 million years ago; fire was collected from natural sources, not made.

description: Joining us from the island of Flores in Indonesia, a relative who stood about 1.1 meters tall. Everyone calls them the Hobbit, and scientists still argue over how they got so small. Do not underestimate this one.
facts: They may have eaten Stegodon, an extinct dwarf relative of elephants, and they shared the island with giant Komodo dragons.
Their brains were about a third the size of ours, and they still made and used stone tools.
punchline: Dodged Komodo dragons, sized up mini elephants. Your last date complained about parking.

anatomy.female: Medium brown skin, dark hair, modest body hair. Tiny: about 1.06 m and 30 kg, small but sturdy, wide pelvis, short legs, relatively long arms, shoulders hunched forward, very long flat feet. Small skull, receding forehead, brow ridge, no chin, relatively large teeth. Wears a woven plant-fibre wrap fully covering the chest and a plant-fibre loincloth.
anatomy.male: Medium brown skin, dark hair and sparse beard, modest body hair. Tiny: estimated about 1.10 m and 32 kg, small but sturdy, wide pelvis, short legs, relatively long arms, shoulders hunched forward, very long flat feet. Small skull, receding forehead, brow ridge, no chin, relatively large teeth. Bare-chested, wearing a woven plant-fibre loincloth.

sources.claim: Homo floresiensis: 100,000-50,000 years ago, 106 cm, 30 kg, small brain, stone tools, Stegodon, Komodo dragons, Hobbit nickname.
Stegodon butchery at Liang Bua was first credited to H. floresiensis but is now linked to later Homo sapiens; floresiensis may still have eaten Stegodon meat.

description: Meet Handy Man, one of the earliest members of our own genus, from eastern and southern Africa. Small, with long, strong arms, habilis got famous as the first toolmaker. Well. About that.
facts: The oldest stone tools claimed so far, from Lomekwi in Kenya, are about 3.3 million years old, roughly 900,000 years older than the oldest Homo habilis, though some researchers question their age.
Habilis shared Africa with Homo erectus for about half a million years.
The most complete habilis skeleton found so far, about 2 million years old, belonged to someone weighing only 31 to 33 kilograms.
punchline: Took credit for someone else's tools. We've all dated one.

anatomy.female: Dark brown skin under a light covering of short dark body hair; dark hair. About 1.05 m and 30 kg, light build, long strong arms, short legs, limb proportions more ape-like than ours, upright. Rounder braincase than australopiths, small brow ridge, smaller face and teeth, projecting lower face, flat broad nose, no chin. Wears a simple hide wrap fully covering the chest and a hide loincloth.
anatomy.male: Dark brown skin under a light covering of short dark body hair; dark hair. About 1.30 m and 37 kg, light, wiry build, long strong arms, short legs, limb proportions more ape-like than ours, upright. Rounder braincase than australopiths, small brow ridge, smaller face and teeth, projecting lower face, flat broad nose, no chin. Bare-chested, wearing a hide loincloth.

sources.claim: Homo habilis lived 2.4-1.4 million years ago, had long arms, and coexisted with Homo erectus for about half a million years.
The oldest known stone tools are 3.3 million years old, older than the genus Homo.
Lomekwi 3 stone tools, West Turkana, Kenya, 3.3 million years ago.
KNM-ER 64061, about 2.04 million years old, weighed an estimated 30.7-32.7 kg.
Domínguez-Rodrigo and Alcalá question whether the Lomekwi 3 tools come from the 3.3-million-year-old layers.

description: Our most famous guest tonight. Lucy was found in Ethiopia in 1974 and has been the poster girl for human evolution ever since. She walked upright, but she never gave up the trees.
facts: The team named Lucy at a party in camp the night she was found, with the Beatles' "Lucy in the Sky with Diamonds" playing over and over.
Footprints at Laetoli in Tanzania, about 3.66 million years old, are the oldest widely accepted trail of upright walking.
One 2016 study suggests Lucy died after falling from a tall tree, though other scientists dispute it.
punchline: Lucy may have fallen hard for someone. Out of a tree, if one study is right.

anatomy.female: Pale pinkish-beige skin on the face, ears, hands and feet, much lighter than the dense dark brown body hair, like a chimpanzee's. About 1.05 m and 29 kg, Lucy-sized: long arms with fingertips reaching the knees, short legs, cone-shaped ribcage, upright stance. Small braincase a third of ours, low forehead, brow ridge, flat nose, strongly projecting jaws, no chin. Wears a simple hide wrap fully covering the chest and a hide loincloth.
anatomy.male: Pale pinkish-beige skin on the face, ears, hands and feet, much lighter than the dense dark brown body hair, like a chimpanzee's. About 1.51 m and 42 kg, much bigger than females: long powerful arms with fingertips reaching the knees, short legs, curved fingers, cone-shaped ribcage, upright stance. Small braincase a third of ours, low forehead, brow ridge, flat nose, strongly projecting jaws, no chin. Bare-chested, wearing a hide loincloth.

sources.claim: A. afarensis lived 3.85-2.95 million years ago; size, brain, face; Lucy found at Hadar in 1974; Laetoli footprints.
Lucy was named during a camp celebration while the Beatles song played.
Lucy's fractures may come from a fall out of a tall tree (Kappelman et al. 2016).

description: We're deep in the family album now. Ardi lived in Ethiopia 4.4 million years ago, and her team thinks she climbed trees and walked upright on the ground. They place her in woodland, which would upend the old idea that walking upright began on open savanna. Some geologists say her home was more open, so keep an open mind.
facts: Ardi's big toe stuck out to the side and could grip branches, while the rest of her foot was stiff enough for walking upright.
Ardi was found in 1994, but the team took 15 years to publish her.
Males had small canine teeth, which some scientists read as a sign of less fighting between males.
punchline: Fifteen years before going public. Still faster than some of your exes.

anatomy.female: Pale pinkish-beige skin on the face, ears, hands and feet, much lighter than the dense black body hair, like a chimpanzee's. About 1.20 m and 50 kg, long arms, very long curved fingers, short legs, a grasping big toe splayed out like a thumb, upright but slightly crouched. Chimp-sized braincase, brow ridge, projecting face, small canines, flat nose. Wears a simple hide wrap fully covering the chest and a hide loincloth.
anatomy.male: Pale pinkish-beige skin on the face, ears, hands and feet, much lighter than the dense black body hair, like a chimpanzee's. About 1.25 m, close to female size, long arms, very long curved fingers, short legs, a grasping big toe splayed out like a thumb, upright but slightly crouched. Chimp-sized braincase, brow ridge, projecting face, small canines barely larger than females', flat nose. Bare-chested, wearing a hide loincloth.

sources.claim: Ardi: 4.4 million years ago, 120 cm, 50 kg, divergent big toe with a rigid foot, small male canines, found 1994 and published 2009, wooded setting.
Cerling et al. argue Ardi's habitat was tree or bush savanna with 5-25% tree cover, not woodland.

description: Our final contestant comes from Chad, roughly 7 million years ago, and may be one of the very first members of the human family. Most of what we know comes from one skull found in 2001. If you've made it this far, I'm impressed, and a little concerned.
facts: "Toumaï" means "hope of life" in Chad's Goran language.

A January 2026 study argues its thigh bone shows it may have walked upright. Critics call the evidence weak: the bone is badly damaged, and some of its features turn up in primates that don't walk upright.
Its brain was about the size of a chimpanzee's, but it had small canine teeth, a trait it shares with later members of the human family.
punchline: "Hope of life." Which is exactly what got this group to stage ten.

anatomy.female: Pale pinkish-beige skin on the face, ears, hands and feet, much lighter than the dense black body hair, like a chimpanzee's. Body barely known: estimated chimp-sized, about 1.10 m and 35 kg, long arms, short legs, possibly upright on two legs (debated). Small chimp-sized braincase, very prominent brow ridge, sloping face with a short midface, small canines. Wears a simple hide wrap fully covering the chest and a hide loincloth.
anatomy.male: Pale pinkish-beige skin on the face, ears, hands and feet, much lighter than the dense black body hair, like a chimpanzee's. Body barely known: estimated chimp-sized, about 1.20 m and 45 kg, long arms, short legs, possibly upright on two legs (debated). Small chimp-sized braincase, very thick, prominent brow ridge, sloping face with a short midface, small canines. Bare-chested, wearing a hide loincloth.

sources.claim: Sahelanthropus: 7-6 million years ago in Chad, found 2001, small brain, prominent brow ridges, small canines, sloping face.
Toumaï means "hope of life" in the local Goran language.
January 2026 Science Advances study argues the femur shows bipedalism; critics call the evidence weak, citing poor preservation and features also seen in nonbipedal primates.
